creator: ethanplusai
title: JARVIS v1 open-sourced on GitHub: a voice orchestration layer on a Mac with read access to Apple Calendar/Mail/Reminders/Notes, browser and terminal control, spawns Claude Code for builds, plus a 'fix yourself' self-editing mode and a settings tab for API keys

tools.name: JARVIS (ethanplusai/jarvis)
tools.detail: live on his GitHub; stripped of personalization so anyone can adapt it; V1

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: JARVIS spawns Claude Code in the background for coding tasks

tools.name: Apple Calendar / Mail / Reminders / Notes
tools.detail: read access, can add notes and calendar events

claims: Capabilities (spoken by JARVIS): open terminals and Chrome, browse the web, spawn Claude Code, create project folders, check git status, plan the day from calendar and tasks, take screenshots, manage to-dos, read email and notes, remember facts, work on any desktop project
'Fix yourself' mode lets JARVIS edit its own repo while you talk through changes -- warning that the backend server may go down
Settings tab for managing API keys
how_to_steps: Clone the JARVIS repo from the creator's GitHub
Add API keys in the quick settings tab
Talk to it; use 'fix yourself' or your own coding agent to extend it
on_screen_only: 'POV: You now have access to your own JARVIS' overlay
Green particle-sphere voice UI in a browser window; menu with Settings / Restart Server items (partially legible)
GitHub repo page (ethanplusai/jarvis, low confidence) in last frame; cluttered desktop with many project folders (e.g. 'tiktok-creator-fund', 'instagram', 'brickin...')
Terminal windows with agent logs behind the UI

relevance.why: Haji already liked JARVIS 2.0 from this creator; this is the earlier v1 release announcement with the same architecture

implement_score.why: Only if Haji wants a Mac-local voice front end; JARVIS 2.0 (liked) supersedes this. The 'fix yourself' self-modifying mode is a risk, not a feature, for production use
